questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted to meet new people. I think Erasmus University Rotterdam looked like a great place to meet new people from many different cultures.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language availability, I really wanted to go to an EU country too, for the convenience of it.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved meeting new people and becoming instantly friends. The university did not meet my expectations though. If I could give half points, I would probably give it 7.5.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host university made sure to keep us updated on all the paperwork we would need to fill out (which is quite a lot) and it was relatively easy to navigate their website for all the information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Again, the university's website has a lot of information upon arrival and we received a few emails telling us what to do and when.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I would love to give it 3.5-4, but I give it 3 because the orientation and assistance stopped with paperwork. The orientation days (introduction days) were lacking and I went home feeling like I didn't really get to know anyone. The days were too short and there were too few. There weren't really any "meet other exchange students" events in the early days, which I feel, affected my overall experience.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: SO so difficult!! I got scammed a month before arrival. I also had to find roommates and trust them without knowing them. We signed our contract two weeks before arrival. It was so stressful, so start looking early. And don't expect the university to help!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's expensive and it's difficult to get. Try to find other exchange students that you feel like you can trust and find a place with them. Or search for apartments that are looking for new roommates. But be aware, many landlords don't want short-stay students (6 months or less) or they don't want non-Dutch.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Horrible experience. I was a few days away from withdrawing from the exchange programme because I didn't have housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Their website for course registration is fairly easy to navigate. Once all the courses for the term are available, you go to the website and pick five (I think it's five) courses that you want to take per term. They also have a calendar that is easy to navigate, so you can see if your classes will overlap.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If you had any issues or you were assigned to classes that ended up overlapping, the exchange office is quick to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Out of six classes in total, I think I might have gotten four classes that I wanted, so that's fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know if I have any advice.. It makes sense and it is pretty easy to do.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I don't feel like I learnt anything new this semester, and that is given I also took introductory courses. The level of education here feels very low compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Their courses are structured in such a way that the students do the most of the work and prepare a lot from home, and the teachers "sum it up" at the university. Except at the actual classes you're just doing group work, group presentation, and repeat. They love group work here, and you don't really get a change to show in-class what you can do. I think I've had more group work here in one semester than I've had at UCPH in all my semesters. 
At UCPH we are sometimes in groups, but our education is not dependant on group work and the ability of your group members. I feel like my grade/what I learn depends on my peers here, and I am not really a fan of that. 
At UCPH we often prepare readings from home and go to either a lecture or a class, or sometimes both, and the teacher go through everything and elaborate. They don't do that here. You do all the work from home - I've watched full-on lectures at home as preparation for class - where the teacher would say "You've already read this" and skip through it to get to the group work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Feeling Orange (you have to take that as an exchange student)
Communication Management
Technology, Media, and Identity
Communication Ethics
Intercultural Communication
Communication Technologies and Their Impact

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If I had to pick one I would recommend Technology, Media, And Identity. That was the only course where I felt challenged and felt like I was learning something new - or at least was learning something that was useful and relevant.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spend a lot of time on public transport because I live far away and the weather is often bad. I would've loved to just use my bike to get around.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out and grocery shopping is cheaper than Copenhagen!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They don't have anything specifically for exchange students (and if they do, they don't really advertise it!) but they have a lot of sports facilities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a sports building with fitness equipment, classes and a tennis course. There are some student activities sometimes, but nothing I looked into as I preferred to do stuff with exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the students bars, go on trips around the country and see other cute Dutch cities!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rotterdam doesn't have a lot of stuff to see, but go to Amsterdam, Delft, Den Haag, Utrecht and perhaps another country. The Netherlands is located right in the middle of everything and a trip to London or Antwerpen doesn't take that long. The smaller Dutch cities have a lot of culture and they're perfect for day-trips to see something else than Rotterdam.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It is in many ways like Copenhagen and Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Local students tend to keep to themselves, so focus on exchange students. the local student you meet often already have their friend-groups and they're friendly enough in class, but I never experienced them wanting to hang out after class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: In many ways it reminds me of Danish culture. But I do appreciate how they party and keep the streets alive.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of their attendance rules (especially if you plan to do a lot of travelling). 
Try to find housing close to the university, as it is a nice place to meet up with friends for a beer or coffee & lunch after class or on a random Tuesday. 
Take a look at the work-load for the courses and how they divide it. Do you want to spend your time doing four group papers or do you want to write one individual assignment and take one exam?

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I met a lot of other people from all over the world and we have friendship that will last for a long time. Going on exchange is a personal journey and you get to know yourself in new ways. It is so rewarding to go on exchange and just say "yes" to everything.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to a new city and a new way of doing things. In many ways Denmark and Netherlands are alike, but sometimes I found myself missing the way things are done in Denmark/at UCPH.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
